title: Fragmentation locality and free-list tombstone diagnostics
content:
Context and motivation:

High-level: we keep seeing noisy, short-lived OOM clusters on the 40GB A100 pools that correlate with periods of high tail latency and a spike in cudaMalloc retries. The pattern is not classic slow leak — total allocs/deallocs balance over 10s windows — but the GPU resident set becomes unusable because of poor locality and many small free regions that can't satisfy medium-sized workspace requests. This note is an exploratory capture of hypotheses, lightweight experiments, and quick diagnostics for free-list tombstones and locality-driven fragmentation.

Observed symptoms (field):
- Periodic surge of cudaMalloc retry logs (~20s windows) followed by successful fallbacks to smaller model variants.
- nvprof/nsys traces show many small cudaMalloc/cudaFree pairs within the same kernel epoch.
- tail latency correlates with a drop in contiguous free region size metric (free_contig_max) collected from mempool telemetry.
- Eviction/defrag attempts (our cooperative defrag) run but often only reclaim 10-20% of the needed contiguous space.

Hypothesis summary (ranked):
1) Free-list tombstones: allocator marks many small freed blocks as tombstones to avoid expensive coalescing on hot path; tombstones accumulate and prevent forming large contiguous spans.
2) Locality inversion: kernels allocate many small temp buffers interleaved with large KV cache allocations; allocator bins cause interleaved placements so coalescing is infeasible.
3) Defrag scheduling mismatch: background defrag runs at low priority and misses short fragmentation windows; when it finally runs, the active working set moved and reclamation is low-value.
4) CUDA driver retry behavior: cudaMallocAsync/streams interactions cause allocation stalls when the allocator attempts to satisfy contig large requests and sees many small freelist entries.

What data we need next (quick list):
- Per-GPU timeline: free_count_by_size_bin (1KB, 4KB, 16KB, 64KB, 256KB, 1MB, 8MB) sampled at 1s
- free_contig_max and free_contig_histogram per epoch
- allocator-op latencies (malloc/free) distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- number of tombstone entries (if we instrument them) and age distribution
- trace of kernel allocation sites (file:line) for hotspots

Quick instrumentation changes to capture: (cheap/low-risk)
- Add a per-bin tombstone counter emitted every 1s (bin id and count).
- Emit a free_contig_max gauge that is computed lazily during sampling (expensive but acceptable at 1s).
- Annotate allocator metadata with provenance tag (kv-cache|workspace|scratch|other) on allocs > 64KB to track interleaving.

Light experiments and findings (short runs):
1) Micro-repro: launch synthetic benchmark with pattern: (big alloc 32MB, many small allocs 16KB x 2048, free in alternating order). On master: observe free_contig_max collapse to <8MB and subsequent big alloc fail path triggers cudaMalloc retry. With coalescing-on-free patch (local test): contiguous spans recovered and retries disappear.
- Metrics: Without coalesce: free_contig_max median 6.3MB, cudaMalloc retry count 42/3000 calls. With coalesce: free_contig_max median 31.5MB, retries 2/3000.

2) Defrag timing tweak: run background defrag every 5s vs 30s. Short experiment (10 minutes) on 4 GPUs under mixed load. Result: 5s schedule reduced tail OOM events by 70%, but increased host CPU usage and occasional stalls when defrag ran concurrently with heavy kernel launches. Conclusion: more aggressive defrag helps but needs smarter preemption.

3) Tombstone aging policy: in microbench we created tombstones for freed blocks kept for 30s before coalescing in bulk. Reducing tombstone age to 2s improved contiguous span formation but increased runtime coalesce overhead by ~8%.

Telemetry excerpts (sanitized):
- sample: gpu-3 @2024-10-28T16:14:12
  free_contig_max: 7.2MB
  free_bins: [128, 340, 1024, 64, 8, 2, 0]
  tombstone_count: 184
  malloc_p95_ms: 1.3
  cudaMallocRetryCount: 18

- sample: gpu-3 @2024-10-28T16:14:32 (after defrag)
  free_contig_max: 29.6MB
  tombstone_count: 12
  cudaMallocRetryCount: 0

Preliminary root-cause model (narrative):
Allocation patterns that are interleaved (large persistent KV caches + many small ephemeral scratch allocations) create fragmentation across the physical address space. Our allocator currently optimizes the fast path by turning some freed regions into "tombstones" and delaying coalescing to avoid locking and slow paths. While this reduces per-op latency under steady-state, it allows the number of non-coalesced fragments to grow during bursty workloads. When a subsequent large request arrives, the allocator must scan many small fragments (negative locality) and often falls back to cudaMalloc (or retries), causing service-level tail latency spikes. Background defrag helps but is scheduled too late and isn't preemptively coordinated with predicted workload transitions.

Actionable changes to try (short list):
- Immediate (safe): reduce tombstone age from 30s -> 5s, enable per-bin coalesce run on low-latency windows. Rollout to canary pool for 48h.
- Mid-term: implement provenance-aware placement: tag persistent KV caches to use a high-density slab that is segregated from ephemeral workspaces so large contiguous spans remain available.
- Scheduler: make defrag opportunistic: trigger defrag at workload quiet points (model-switch events or after checkpoint flushes) and make it preemptible (checkpoint there is an explicit cancel on heavy launch).
- Long-term: consider hybrid allocator mode: fast-path tombstones for tiny bins only, force immediate coalesce for medium/large bins (>=64KB). Also consider integrating a compacting pass that migrates live blocks into new contiguous slab during low activity.

Playbook for on-call (triage steps):
1) Check telemetry: free_contig_max < 16MB and tombstone_count > 100 -> flag fragmentation incident.
2) If fragmentation incident: switch canary pool to tombstone-age=2s config and enable canary defrag schedule (5s).
3) If immediate fix needed: trigger model fallback to smaller variant (automated policy already exists) while diagnostics continue.
4) Collect nsys trace for 60s around incident and capture allocator logs. Attach to PROJ-4521.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Are some GPU drivers compounding fragmentation by not preserving physical locality across cudaFree/cudaMallocAsync? Need to add low-level experiment that allocates pinned host memory and measures physical addresses where possible.
- Cost model: what's the CPU overhead and latency regression if we coalesce eagerly for >=64KB bins? Microbench suggests ~8-12% CPU cost under high churn; is that acceptable for Dedicated customers?
- Can we get kernel-level provenance reliably in release builds without high perf cost?

Next experiments (ordered):
- Canary run with tombstone-age=5s across 10 GPUs for 48h; collect full 1s bin histograms.
- Implementation: per-bin eager coalesce for bins >=64KB under canary, measure malloc latency and CPU.
- Allocate/migrate compacting POC: allocate new slab and copy live buffers during low-traffic window, measure pause and success rate.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Create Jira ticket PROJ-4521 with attached nsys traces and these notes.
- PR: small instrumentation to emit tombstone_count per bin -> PR draft at linked_artifacts.
- Demo plan for infra review: show microbench before/after coalesce patch and defrag schedule tweak.

Appendix: commands and quick scripts used
- nsys profile: sudo nsys profile -o out.qdrep --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=60 --capture-range=nvtx
- mempool dump (dev tool): ./mempool_inspect --gpu 3 --format=json --bins --contig-scan > dump-20241028.json
- microbench invocation: ./fragmentation-microbench --pattern alt-big-small --big-size 33554432 --small-size 16384 --small-count 2048 --duration 300

If folks want to iterate, add notes inline below. I'm going to spin the canary patch next and attach PR link when ready.

-- Anjali
